title: Wavering demand and regional divergence: Q2 black mass review
gist: Benchmark's Q2 2026 black mass review shows recycled battery intermediate payables calming after CIF Asia NCM black mass hit all-time highs of 104.0% (EOL) and 137.5% (production scrap) in May, before easing into a more cautious, regionally fragmented pricing environment as lithium prices began to weaken, per analyst Frederick Bloomfield.

themes.theme: Q2 payable volatility and May peak

insights.claim: Black mass payables were less volatile in Q2 2026 than in Q1, as trading levels for the recycled battery intermediate responded to cooling battery metal markets, wavering demand, and continued regional divergence.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Signals the black mass recycling market entering a calmer, more fragmented phase after a stronger Q1 — relevant for recyclers' margin forecasting.

insights.claim: CIF Asia NCM black mass payables from end-of-life (EOL) batteries and from production scrap hit all-time highs in May 2026 of 104.0% and 137.5% respectively, according to Benchmark's Black Mass Price Assessment.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Record payable percentages above 100% indicate extremely aggressive competition for feedstock in the Asian recycling market — a peak signal for timing recycler feedstock cost exposure.
insights.locator: "The largest movements were recorded in the seaborne Asia market..."

insights.claim: By the end of Q2 2026, black mass payables had eased from May's highs as the market shifted from broad strength to a more cautious, regionally fragmented pricing environment while lithium prices began to show weakness.
insights.speaker: Frederick Bloomfield, senior price analyst at Benchmark
insights.so_what: Links black mass payable weakness directly to softening lithium prices — a leading or coincident indicator investors can track between the two markets.
insights.quote: The quarter saw a clear shift from broad strength towards a more cautious and regionally fragmented pricing environment as lithium prices began to show weakness.

insights.claim: Black mass pricing in Q2 2026 diverged by region, with the seaborne Asia market showing by far the largest swings while other regions saw more muted moves, reflecting a broader shift toward regional fragmentation in recycled battery material markets.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Regional divergence implies differentiated risk exposure depending on which regional black mass market a recycler or trader is exposed to.
